overallSummary: Fabio Giglietto maintains a strong, scholarly social media presence across academic and professional platforms (LinkedIn, Bluesky, and Mastodon) with a combined audience of 3,580 followers. Content primarily focuses on computational social science, platform governance, coordinated inauthentic behavior, and research/hiring announcements. Engagement across all platforms is healthy, driven by major milestone updates such as new publications, grant awards, and tool releases.

contentThemes.description: Research findings, tools (CooRnet), and conference talks focused on detecting coordinated manipulation campaigns.
Announcements regarding newly awarded research grants, published papers, and major software releases.
Job postings for postdoctoral researchers and PhD opportunities in computational social science.

recommendations: Cross-promote major research breakthroughs and hiring calls across all three platforms consistently to maximize reach.
Incorporate more visual content (charts, network graphs, screenshots of CooRnet v2.0) to boost post visibility and engagement.
Engage with comments actively on LinkedIn and Bluesky to build community discussions around methodology and academic open roles.

platformInsights.bluesky: Achieves the highest engagement rate (averaging ~5.8%), driven by strong resharing/reposting of publications and educational opportunities.
platformInsights.mastodon: Serves as an effective niche platform for technical and methodological discussions with an engaged open-source academic community.
platformInsights.linkedin: Generates the highest raw interaction counts (likes and comments) particularly around high-impact professional milestones like grant funding and hiring announcements.

topPerformingContent.content: Just published our new paper on coordinated inauthentic behavior on social media platforms!
Excited to announce that our research team has been awarded a new grant to study information operations across social media platforms.
Our team has just released v2.0 of CooRnet, with improved algorithms for detecting coordinated link sharing behavior.
